question: Do exact pairs decide the full named next ordinary birth roster on lawful reached not-all-equal stages?
primary_observable: Named holder parent-support and fresh-count multiset and scalar next-cut outcome on every certified table orbit, uniform and recursive inherited fractions separately. Twenty-eight-name inversion, loose names and witnesses, explosive first and second reached stages, parity controls.
forbidden_inputs: Birth ages, named source and word count as supplied pair-table information; identifying a shared old slot by fiat; confusing observed pair equality, a necessary invariant, a class guarantee and universal determination.
cheapest_meaningful_control: Known physical four-place founder at width 28, physical count four; closed eight-name uniform NAE alternatives; known equal-state/different-count parity controls; small literal-word comparisons.
first_executable_signal: Compute two exact 28-name tables from the 16-name predecessor, the actual complete named cut and necessary constraints on unrestricted unmarked rivals. Then proceed to general proof and explosive census, followed by inherited-weight verdicts.
resource_budget: Six GiB per process, one BLAS thread. Full ring founder class with at most 17 names; pairs of these and single small companions; exact interval-free competitor tests; prior registration before checks exceeding ten minutes. Two independent 64-draw panels per law.
stop_rule: Full reached theorem or minimum scoped live counterexample; otherwise largest proved class with complete finite explosive founder and next-cut roster census, exact pair comparison, any unresolved pair hypotheses explicit.
decision_or_followup_rule: Distinguish arbitrary and genuinely reached rivals, named parent profiles from counts, every stage from tested cohorts, uniform-law inheritance from inherited-state weighting. Leave an independent referee handoff, no successor work.
